analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches, documentation and metadata against the indexed model and selected detailed T-041 evidence. EngineV2KVBackendPolicy.swift head 38–42 adds only the exact Flint artifact to automatic paging; explicit selections, kill-switch parsing, capability vetoes and automatic-failure fallback remain unchanged. No demonstrated admission or authorization bypass follows from that selection.
FlintAnswerStopConstraint.swift added head 70–92 introduces mask caching and delegates chained-decode eligibility. Its existing allowedTokenIDs (base 55–67) supports sharing masks across scanning nodes with the same base state regardless of stop progress, and a distinct matched mask. Existing bounded interning and fail-closed transitions remain. No concrete regression is established locally.
docs/architecture/inference.md 2172–2183 describes speculative constrained sampling, RNG/penalty restoration, cached masks and increased default serving width. These implementation claims require integration verification, not reliance on prose. Relevant contracts are output integrity (T-007/TB-007), consumer-triggered resource exhaustion, cancellation (T-010), and residual/cache isolation (T-028/T-041). Surrounding documentation retains encryption, media ownership, admission and qualification boundaries; no visible change affects keys, attestation, billing or fan authority.
Material remaining review: inspect the SDK delta 889fe3c→cbaf4cc in libs/mlx-swift-lm, the base Flint constraint, and SDK mask-cache/chaining consumers. Verify negative key -1 is supported and constraint-local, cached masks remain valid after exhaustion, speculative tokens cannot transition or emit before confirmation, and redraw restores sampling state. Trace actual backend construction and serving-width admission to ensure the newly automatic Flint paging remains physically budgeted. The SDK implementation and these callers are outside this batch; missing source does not establish either safety or a vulnerability.
